Technical Implementation Details: Set up std.socket.TcpSocket. Bind to port 25565 and start listening.
Cryptic Developer Hint: Look into non-blocking sockets early, or a single slow client will freeze your entire main loop.

Technical Implementation Details: Accept incoming client connections and store their socket handles in a client array.
Cryptic Developer Hint: A closed socket can look like a successful read of 0 bytes. Don't loop infinitely on dead pipes.

Technical Implementation Details: Read the first byte. Verify it matches packet ID 0x00. Read the username string.
Cryptic Developer Hint: Minecraft Classic strings are always fixed to 64 bytes, padded with spaces (0x20). Strip them carefully.

Technical Implementation Details: Construct and send response 0x00, followed immediately by 0x02 (Level Initialize).
Cryptic Developer Hint: Endianness matters. Dlang defaults to host order, but network bytes demand big-endian format.

Technical Implementation Details: Allocate a 1D block array (e.g., 64x64x64). Compress blocks or chunk them into 0x03 packets.
Cryptic Developer Hint: The map data packet (0x03) requires a length header and Gzip compression. Mind the 1024-byte chunk limit.

Technical Implementation Details: Listen for packet 0x05 (Player Position). Update server state and echo to other clients.
Cryptic Developer Hint: Positions are sent as fixed-point integers (multiplied by 32). Don't parse them as raw floats.

Technical Implementation Details: Refactor packet reading/writing to use stack allocation or manual scope buffers instead of GC.
Cryptic Developer Hint: D's arrays can trigger GC if you append (~=). Use explicit slices over pre-allocated malloc buffers.

Technical Implementation Details: Implement a thread-safe message queue or use vibe.d fibers to handle chat and movement concurrently.
Cryptic Developer Hint: Shared data in D requires explicit synchronization. Look into std.concurrency or lightweight mutexes.
